articleTitle: Principles Of Law For Engineers And Managers

IEE Colloquium on Principles of Law for Engineers and Managers, Part 1 (Digest No: 1996/246)
abstract: Forensic Science is a profession that is well known in connection with criminal cases. It is less well known that the forensic scientists have an engineering counterpart, the forensic engineer who assists in criminal and civil cases that involve some aspects of engineering. Although anyone with some special expertise may act as an expert witness, a forensic engineer is an engineer who is not only a specialist in particular branches of engineering, but also specialises in investigating, reporting and giving evidence in engineering matters in legal disputes. This paper describes the work of the engineering expert witness or forensic engineer and shows when and where one might need such an expert when a dispute arises. Case studies in civil and criminal actions are presented.

abstract: The following questions are discussed: What is a contract? Is there a contract? When did the contract come into being? Whose terms and conditions apply to the Contact? What happens if there is a dispute? Are there defined liabilities for failure to perform the contract where non-performance involves delay and where non-performance involves defects of some sort.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Principles of Law for Engineers and Managers, Part 1 (Digest No: 1996/246)
abstract: Given the broad scope of the competition rules and the potentially serious consequences of infringing those rules, it is important to ensure a degree of familiarity with the law amongst employees and management to reduce the likelihood of inadvertent infringements and to increase the knowledge within the company of the likely penalties for infringement and thus reducing the risk of any intentional infringement of the laws. Both the UK and EC competition laws are briefly reviewed.
